The factsheet does not specify the exact weight variable name (e.g., TOTWGT or W_FSTUWT) or whether replicate weights were used, so the specific weighting implementation cannot be verified from the provided text. Plausible values are used for cognitive achievement reporting in PISA; however, this factsheet presents proficiency levels and mean-score comparisons rather than detailing the PV-combining procedure.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in Israel performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how results relate to trends and subgroup patterns. It reports mean-score comparisons with the OECD average, proficiency-level shares (e.g., Level 2 and Level 5/6), and changes over time (notably 2018–2022 and comparisons to 2012/2015/2006). The assessment uses two two-hour tests with different students receiving different item sets, plus student and school questionnaires; the factsheet also notes that creative thinking and financial literacy were included as special/optional components. For Israel, the factsheet states that all data met PISA quality standards, and it flags that some countries with an asterisk may have sampling-standard issues. The document does not provide the underlying PV-combining or missing-data procedures, and it does not conduct student-level ML modeling.
